subject: Re: MedDevCo - privacy carveout and audit access request
messages:
From: Elena Perez <elena.perez@meddevco.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: security@meddevco.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data residency + audit access requirements for Private deployment

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed, MedDevCo has regulatory obligations that require us to verify control over patient-identifiable data when a vendor hosts our models. Our procurement team requested specifics about the audit scope for the Private (VPC) deployment.

High level asks: 
- Ability to perform an annual on-site audit (or an approved remote equivalent) with access to application logs and file-level artifacts generated during processing.
- Audit window: ability to inspect up to 7 days of historical data on request; the request must be accommodated within a 30-day notice period.
- Option for our third-party auditor (named vendor) to interview engineers and review configuration snapshots.

I attached MedDevCo_Audit_Request_v2.pdf which summarizes the required evidence. From a contract standpoint, we need a clause granting these rights or an auditable alternative. Also please share any associated costs you expect for supporting on-site access.

Elena
Elena Perez
Head of Compliance, MedDevCo
elena.perez@meddevco.com

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Perez <elena.perez@meddevco.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency + audit access requirements for Private deployment

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear note and the attachment. We can support a Private deployment in a US region with in-country data handling, but a few items need alignment with our security and legal model. Quick thoughts: 

- We can provide a read-only audit replica (secure, time-limited access) containing the operational logs and configuration snapshots you mention.
- Full file-level access for third-party auditors is sensitive for us — we typically offer either a controlled on-site review under Redwood supervision or a remote secure session where we surface the requested artifacts (not raw file export).
- We need to understand the frequency and duration you anticipate for on-site audits. Providing 7 days of historical data on request is possible but may mean we ask for either a one-time assistance fee or a commercial concession to cover operational hours.

Looping in Kimberly and Markus to get legal/finance comfort and to request executive approval for any commercial concessions.

Next step: Kimberly, can you share recommended redlines and an approval ask we can send Elena? Markus — is a modest one-time fee or a small up-front discount preferred from a go/no-go perspective?

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Data residency + audit access requirements for Private deployment

Team —

I reviewed MedDevCo_Audit_Request_v2.pdf. Summary and recommended approach: 

1) Audit scope: Agree to provide operational logs, configuration snapshots, and a redacted subset of runtime artifacts. We should avoid granting raw file-level exports.

2) On-site vs remote: Offer a supervised on-site review (max 3 Redwood staff + up to 2 customer auditors) or a secure remote session where we present artifacts via our audit portal.

3) Historical data: Limit historical extract to 14 days of requestable artifacts. MedDevCo asked for 7; legal prefers 14 as a safe compromise for reproduction.

4) Notice window: 45 days notice for on-site audits to accommodate scheduling and capacity.

5) Interview access: Allow interviews with engineers in a supervised format; no access to developer laptops or internal admin consoles.

Commercial: Because this deviates from our standard SOC/remote-only model, request a commercial concession: either a one-time technical assistance fee of $40,000 or a one-time contractual discount equivalent (we can frame this as a 6% credit on the initial 12-month commit).

Approval ask for execs: 
- Approve the above carveouts (14-day history cap, 45-day notice, supervised interview limits).
- Approve commercial concession option up to 6%/one-time $40k credit.

Markus, if you approve, Jordan should be asked to issue the special term and the approved concession in the SOW.

Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency + audit access requirements for Private deployment

Thanks Kimberly — I reviewed and am comfortable with the proposed guardrails. Decision: we will approve the carveouts with a couple of constraints.

Approved concessions (final):
- Historical data window: 14 days (no file-level exports).
- Notice: 45 days for on-site audits.
- Interview: supervised sessions only; max 2 external auditors; no access to developer machines.
- Commercial: approve a one-time concession up to 5% of the first-year committed spend (in lieu of the $40k technical assistance fee).

Jordan: please prepare the special terms wording ("Limited Audit Access; Supervised Review; 14-day Historical Snapshot; 45-day Notice") and include a line for the 5% one-time concession tied to deal RDW-2027-0341. We will not accept raw file-level exports.

Logan, send Elena the approved parameters and the DocuSign link once Jordan has the updated SOW and MAP.

-Markus
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. We can support MedDevCo's Private deployment with the following mutually-agreed parameters: 

- Audit access: Redwood will provide supervised audit reviews (on-site or remote) delivering operational logs, configuration snapshots, and redacted runtime artifacts. We will not provide raw file-level exports.
- Historical window: Up to 14 days of historical artifacts made available on request.
- Notice: 45 days' notice required for any on-site audit.
- Auditor access: Up to 2 external auditors; interviews with engineers are allowed in supervised sessions. 
- Commercial concession: Redwood will apply a one-time 5% credit against the first-year committed spend for RDW-2027-0341 to cover operational support for audits.

Next steps: Jordan Blake from Deal Desk will issue an updated SOW and Mutual Action Plan reflecting these terms and the 5% one-time concession.
